chunks: And by this chain of narration, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), he said:

My father asked for some anointing oil to anoint his head with it. When he had anointed himself, I asked him: 'What is that you have anointed with?' He said: 'It is violet (banafsha).' I asked: 'And what is the virtue/preference of violet?' He said: 'My father narrated to me from my grandfather Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father (peace be upon them all), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The virtue of violet over other oils is like the virtue of Islam over all other religions.'

key_terms.البَنَفْسَجُ: Violet or viola, a type of flower used for oil

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or comparative virtue of violet oil according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* emphasizes the spiritual and physical purity of violet oil, elevating it above other anointing agents just as Islam transcends other faiths. The chain of narration (isnad) underscores the continuous transmission of this virtue through the Ahl al-Bayt, linking Ja'far al-Sadiq directly to the Prophet via Imam al-Husayn and Imam Ali. This comparison serves as a metaphor for the comprehensive excellence of the divine message within Shia theology.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-148 According to the same documentation, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad (a.s.),

“My father asked for some anointment and rubbed it on his face and head. I asked him what it was. He (a.s.) said, “It was viola.” I asked him, “What makes viola the best?” He (a.s.) said, “My father (a.s.) quoted on the authority of my grandfather Al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.), on the authority of his father (a.s.) that God’s Prophet (S) said, ‘Viola is the best anointment as Islam is the best religion.’”
